segments.oily: Reviewers with oily t-zone areas or combination-oily skin describe the serum as non-greasy and not heavy, with one noting it balances an oily r-zone alongside dry spots.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin, including seasonal winter dryness, report the serum leaves skin hydrated, softer and less dull without causing irritation.
segments.combination: Reviewers with combination skin (including combination dry/oily) report the serum evens tone and adds brightness without feeling oily or greasy, especially useful for winter dullness.
segments.sensitive: Reviewers who identify as having sensitive or acne-prone sensitive skin report good tolerance overall, with several noting no irritation or breakouts, though one reviewer with sensitive skin experienced burning and redness.
segments.mature: A 61-year-old reviewer with sun-damaged, mature skin reports reduced redness and improved appearance, calling it the best result she has seen outside a dermatologist's office.

concerns.aging: Reviewers focused on firmness and elasticity report skin looking plumper, tighter and smoother after a few days to weeks; one mature reviewer with 60 years of sun damage calls it the best product she's used for overall skin appearance.
concerns.dehydration: Reviewers report the serum feels hydrating, lightweight and non-sticky, waking up with moisturized, firm skin; one reviewer specifically credits it with preventing flakiness after 12 hours of wear.
concerns.redness: Two reviewers report visible reduction in facial redness, including one who states cheek redness disappeared; no reports of increased redness from regular use, though one reviewer experienced burning and irritation.
concerns.barrier: One reviewer reports the serum corrected bumps and redness likely linked to hormonal changes after a single use, alongside her existing moisturizer; no other reviewers describe barrier-specific effects.
concerns.spots: The large majority of reviewers report fading of dark spots, hyperpigmentation, sun spots and post-acne marks within one to three weeks of use; a few note it is too soon to judge or have not yet seen changes on their dark spots.
concerns.blemishes: Several reviewers with acne-prone or breakout-prone skin report no new breakouts and fading acne scars/spots, with one noting it is the first vitamin C serum that hasn't caused breakouts; one reviewer instead reports the serum burns and irritates her skin.
concerns.oiliness: Reviewers describe the texture as lightweight and non-greasy, layering well under makeup without feeling oily, including those who identify as combination or oily-prone.

extraits.titre: Serum burns face + ignore "gifted by Tatcha" reviews
extraits.texte: Tatcha is filled with reviews from influencers who received free "gifted" items especially for new products so it's hard to know what real paying customers think. I've used Tatcha for years and like many of their products. This one however burns on my face and leaves it irritated and red for hours. The dispenser also isn't designed properly so the serum runs down the side of the bottle. I will not be repurchasing. Tatcha, can you please add a filter in your reviews to filter verified purchases vs "gifted by Tatcha" reviews? This will give the company and reviews more credibility. If a product is good, customers will write honest positive reviews!
